what_its_for: Calcipotriene is used to treat plaque psoriasis, a skin condition that causes thick, scaly, red patches on the skin. It works like a form of vitamin D to slow down the overgrowth of skin cells that causes these patches.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a cream, ointment, foam, or scalp solution. Wash and dry your hands before and after applying. Apply a thin layer only to the affected skin areas. Rub it in gently. Do NOT apply to your face, groin, armpits, or inside skin folds unless your doctor specifically tells you to. If using the scalp solution or foam, part your hair and apply directly to the scalp. Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or nose. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water.
dosing: Typically apply once or twice daily, as directed by your doctor. Do not use more than your doctor prescribes. In most cases, adults should not use more than 100 grams per week of the cream or ointment. Follow your doctor's instructions carefully.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT apply extra medicine to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat and direct sunlight. Do not freeze. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid applying to your face, eyes, mouth, or sensitive skin areas unless told to by your doctor. Avoid using more than the recommended amount, as overuse can raise calcium levels in your blood. Avoid prolonged sun exposure on treated areas, and do not use tanning beds or sunlamps. Avoid using other skin products on treated areas unless your doctor approves. Avoid contact with the eyes.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you experience: signs of high calcium in your blood such as nausea, vomiting, constipation, unusual thirst, frequent urination, muscle weakness, or confusion; severe skin irritation, burning, redness, or peeling at the application site; no improvement in your skin after 8 weeks of treatment; or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may start to see improvement in your skin within 2 to 4 weeks of regular use. The full benefit usually takes about 6 to 8 weeks. Keep using the medicine as directed even if improvement is slow. Do not stop without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Children: Safety and dosing in children under 12 years old has not been fully established. Children may absorb more of this medicine through their skin and are at higher risk for side effects. Use only under close medical supervision. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine. It is not fully known if it is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Older adults: Use with caution. Elderly patients may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine. Patients with kidney disease or history of high calcium levels: Use with extra caution and inform your doctor, as this medicine can affect calcium levels in the body.
